# RID-specific .NET runtime asset sample

`app.deps.json` and `app.dll` were generated by publishing the included .NET 10 app against a
local NuGet package. `make_package.py` packages the managed DLL from the
sibling `dotnet-managed-assembly` fixture as two RID-specific runtime assets.
The output preserves the `runtimes/<rid>/lib/...` paths described by the
[.NET runtime configuration format](https://github.com/dotnet/dotnet/blob/main/src/sdk/documentation/specs/runtime-configuration-file.md).
The package ID and version differ from the assembly name and version by design.

From this directory, regenerate the manifest and DLLs with:

```sh
python3 make_package.py
fixture_packages="$(mktemp -d)"
NUGET_PACKAGES="$fixture_packages" dotnet restore app/app.csproj --source "$(pwd)/feed" -p:NuGetAudit=false
NUGET_PACKAGES="$fixture_packages" dotnet publish app/app.csproj -c Release --no-restore -o published
cp published/app.deps.json published/app.dll .
cp published/runtimes/linux-x64/lib/net10.0/Acme.Runtime.dll runtimes/linux-x64/lib/net10.0/Acme.Runtime.dll
cp published/runtimes/osx-arm64/lib/net10.0/Acme.Runtime.dll runtimes/osx-arm64/lib/net10.0/Acme.Runtime.dll
```

The generated package and `feed` directory are build outputs. Tests read the
checked-in manifest and DLLs without requiring the .NET SDK in CI.
